the Dashboard architecture context file exists and is consistent with the affected component, but the strategy does not cite specific files/APIs. | ", "artifacts/epic-tasks/RHAISTRAT-9017-E001.md": "--- epic_id: RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 title: Keyboard operability and focus indicator fixes for four audited Dashboard flows parent_strat: RHAISTRAT-9017 component: Dashboard team: RHOAI Dashboard type: Implementation priority: P1 dependencies: [] ai_signals: change_specificity: 1 pattern_precedent: 1 adapter_pattern: 0 existing_foundation: 1 open_questions: 1 external_dependency: 1 human_process_gates: 1 repo_access: 1 architecture_claims: 0 implementation_type: null investigation_signals: null ai_implementability: High ai_implementability_score: 7 jira_key: «redacted» null gated_by: null gate_failure_impact: null --- # Keyboard operability and focus indicator fixes for four audited Dashboard flows ## Description This epic remediates the keyboard accessibility defects found by the accessibility audit in the four core Dashboard flows: project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, and pipeline run submission. It delivers a Dashboard in which each of these flows can be completed end to end using the keyboard alone, with no focus traps, no unreachable controls, and consistent visible focus indicators across all interactive controls. The audit report enumerates the exact defects per flow; this epic fixes that enumerated list. ## Scope - Fix focus loss in modals used by the four audited flows (focus moved to the dialog on open, trapped while open, returned to the invoking control on close). - Make every control in the four audited flows reachable and operable by keyboard (tab order, arrow-key navigation where the widget pattern requires it, escape/cancel behavior). - Remove any keyboard focus traps and dead-end navigation states in the audited flows. - Apply a consistent visible focus indicator style across all interactive controls in the audited flows (modals, forms, toolbars, tables, menus). - Verify each defect enumerated in the audit report for the four flows is addressed; defects outside the audited flows and screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require are out of scope. - Update any captions, screenshots, or references in the Dashboard that fall out of these fixes (no new content authored). ## Acceptance Criteria - Each of the four audited flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission) can be completed start to finish using only the keyboard, verified by a manual keyboard-only walkthrough of each flow. - No focus traps exist in the audited flows: focus entering a modal stays within it while open and returns to the invoking control on close. - Every control presented in the audited flows is reachable via keyboard and operable without a pointing device. - A visible focus indicator appears on every interactive control in the audited flows, using one consistent indicator treatment across all four flows. - Every defect itemized in the audit report for the four audited flows is checked off as fixed or explicitly dispositioned with rationale. ## HLR Traceability - HLR-1 (P1): The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard, with no focus traps or unreachable controls. - HLR-2 (P1): Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited flows. The updated conformance statement is a renewal requirement from two public-sector customers, so the published documents are a deliverable of this strategy in their own right. The documentation work must reflect only what the keyboard remediation actually delivered, staying within the strategy's out-of-scope boundaries (screen-reader semantics beyond the keyboard fixes and flows outside the four audited ones). ## Scope - Update the VPAT (conformance statement) to reflect the remediated keyboard operability and focus indicator state of the four audited flows. - Update the product documentation accessibility statement to describe the current supported state, including the scope of the audited flows and any remaining known limitations that fall outside this strategy's fixes. - Republish both documents through the Red Hat docs content process so the public conformance statement is current. - Obtain technical review of the updated claims against the implemented fixes before publication. ## Acceptance Criteria - The VPAT is updated so its conformance claims for the four audited flows match the remediated state, with no claims covering the out-of-scope items (screen-reader semantics beyond the keyboard fixes, flows outside the four audited ones). - The accessibility statement in the product documentation is updated and republished. - The updated documentation has been technically reviewed against the implemented keyboard fixes, with review sign-off recorded. - Both documents are republished and publicly available in their updated form. ## HLR Traceability - HLR-3 (P2): The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed state, with technical review. Although the strategy is S-sized with audit-enumerated defects and no open questions, it spans two architecturally distinct work streams that warrant separate PR review cycles: Dashboard code implementation (keyboard operability and focus indicator fixes) and substantive content authoring (VPAT conformance statement and accessibility statement republish). Per the multiple-distinct-work-streams escape condition, full decomposition applies. ## Epic List | ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority | |-------|-------|------|------|----------| | RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 | Keyboard operability and focus indicator fixes for four audited Dashboard flows | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P1 | | RHAISTRAT-9017-E002 | Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and accessibility statement) | Implementation | RHOAI Documentation | P2 | ## Dependency DAG ```mermaid graph TD E001[RHAISTRAT-9017-E001
Keyboard + focus fixes] --> E002[RHAISTRAT-9017-E002
VPAT / docs republish] ``` ## DAG Justification | Edge | Rule | Rationale | |------|------|-----------| | E001 → E002 | Rule 11 (docs-authoring blocked by all Implementation epics) | The VPAT and accessibility statement describe the fixed state of the four flows, so the documentation epic must be blocked by the Dashboard implementation epic. Per the docs-authoring priority exception, this edge does not push E002's P2 upstream: E001 is P1 on its own HLRs (HLR-1, HLR-2). | No Investigation epics: the strategy's Open Questions section states "None — the audit report enumerates the exact defects per flow," and no conditional ADRs, pending reviews, or assumptions requiring technical resolution appear elsewhere in the strategy. ## HLR Traceability Matrix | HLR | Priority | Epic | Coverage | |-----|----------|------|----------| | HLR-1 | P1 | RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 | Keyboard operability of the four audited flows (no focus traps, no unreachable controls) | | HLR-2 | P1 | RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 | Consistent visible focus indicators across the audited flows | | HLR-3 | P2 | RHAISTRAT-9017-E002 | VPAT and accessibility statement updated and republished with technical review | Full HLR coverage: HLR-1, HLR-2, and HLR-3 each map to exactly one epic; no orphaned requirements. ### Boundary and bundling decisions - **HLR-1 + HLR-2 bundled into E001**: both HLRs target the same component (Dashboard), same team (RHOAI Dashboard), and the same UI surfaces (the four audited flows). They are one logical accessibility-remediation change — focus-trap removal, control reachability, and focus-indicator consistency are fixed together on the same modals and controls. Splitting them would make two epics touch the same UI surface and add an artificial serialization edge. - **HLR-3 as a separate docs-authoring epic (E002)**: updating and republishing the VPAT and the product accessibility statement is substantive content authoring with a different review cycle (Red Hat docs content process, technical review) than the Dashboard code fixes — a distinct work stream, not an incidental documentation touch-up falling out of the code change. - **E002 priority**: docs-authoring priority exception — strategy frontmatter `priority: Normal` → P2. The edge from E001 does not raise E001 above the P1 it inherits from HLR-1/HLR-2. ## Health Warnings - **Missing strategy sections (non-blocking)**: the strategy has no Impacted Teams table, no Dependencies table, no Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, no Non-Functional Requirements, and no size field. Owner teams were inferred: RHOAI Dashboard from the Dashboard architecture context file; the documentation epic's owner (RHOAI Documentation) is assumed and should be confirmed before execution. - **Scope note on the conformance statement**: a VPAT typically covers the whole product, while this strategy fixes only the four audited flows and explicitly excludes screen-reader semantics and all other flows. The documentation epic must scope the updated conformance claims to what was actually remediated so the published statement is not overclaiming; reviewers should verify the statement wording against the out-of-scope list. - **No priority inversions detected**: P1 code fixes, P2 documentation — consistent with the docs being a follow-on deliverable. ## Tiered Delivery Not applicable — no external dependencies with uncertain timing. Both public- sector customer deliverables (fixes and published VPAT) are produced by this decomposition's two epics. E001's values are consistent with the strategy and rationales: change_specificity +1 (audit enumerates exact defects, four flows named), pattern_precedent +1 (PatternFly widget patterns in the same codebase), existing_foundation +1 (remediation of existing flows), open_questions +1 (strategy says none), human_process_gates +1 (normal code review only). Signal rationales in both ai-signals files match the frontmatter values. (Arithmetic/thresholds not checked per review rules.) ### 6. Acceptance Criteria Quality (2/2) E001's ACs are testable: keyboard-only walkthrough per named flow, focus-trap behavior (trap while open, return on close), control reachability, one consistent focus indicator treatment, and a per-defect checklist with explicit disposition. E002's ACs include the rule-mandated technical-review AC for docs-authoring (sign-off recorded), plus no-overclaim verification against the out-of-scope list and republished-publicly checks. No external-schedule constraints misfiled as ACs. Neither epic body references sibling epics by draft ID. E001 is defect remediation, not a component replacement, so no rollback/feature-flag AC is mandated; no konflux chain exists. ### 7. Completeness (2/2) Full scope coverage: keyboard operability and focus indicators for the four audited flows (E001), VPAT plus accessibility-statement update, technical review, and republication (E002). Out-of-scope boundaries (screen-reader semantics, other flows) are respected and explicitly encoded in both epics. The stakeholder commitment driving the strategy (public-sector customer renewal requiring the published VPAT) is carried into E002's description. Strategy-level gaps (missing Impacted Teams, no size field, assumed documentation owner) are surfaced in the decomposition's Health Warnings rather than silently dropped, including a substantive warning about scoping VPAT claims to avoid overclaiming.
